bounds.domain: One already sealed capture-only manifest-v3 operation, two abstract chunk identities and two publication executions. Exact claim abstracts the live execution, operation identity, canonical manifest and inventory checks at resolver entry.
bounds.persistence: Catalogue capture and its local receipt are distinct. The resolver can restore the local receipt from the exact captured catalogue claim. One owner holds the local spool lock, and close retains the journal and chunk receipts for a successor. Successful journal writes are atomic in the model.
bounds.conformance: The maintained Bun suite runs the capture pipeline, local key provider, real spool files and publication resolver. It interrupts the capture callback before local acknowledgement, rejects a mismatching catalogue without confirming the journal, and reopens the exact sealed journal. It rejects a live competing owner and incomplete publication, then completes using the previous owner's durable receipt. Catalogue and remote upload receipts are fixture inputs.
bounds.gaps: Covers only the sealed capture-only handoff through local publication receipt. Database claim issuance and renewal, Linux process-death reclamation, storage failures within a write, inline capture/upload, remote object effects, retention, activation and end-to-end restore are outside this model. The linked suite also exercises cleanup, which does not extend the transition proof.

assumptions: The original spool is retained and close only releases the exact local lock. No fairness is needed to preserve existing receipts.
Without fairness, a durable captured catalogue can remain available while publication never resumes.

One exact publication owner is available without further release or interference. Reopen, begin, both successful chunk receipts and completion are weakly fair. Catalogue capture is a premise for progress, and remote or local storage availability is not guaranteed.
